strategy.purpose: Make sure what a pelvic health physio would tell you in the room is with you at home.
strategy.problem: A patient leaves a pelvic health appointment with advice, an exercise program and usually a handout. By the time they need any of it, most is forgotten, lost in an inbox or in a drawer, and the program gets abandoned halfway through a set because they lost count. The clinician then spends the next appointment repeating the last one.

audiences.name: Pelvic health physiotherapists
audiences.need: Patients who follow the program between visits, without more admin.
audiences.context: They subscribe, and set each patient up from a computer with their own programs, advice and exercises from the library. Their patients get six months free. They meet Pelvy through a demo with Amelia.

audiences.name: GPs, specialists and other clinicians
audiences.need: Something sound to recommend when a patient cannot get to a pelvic health physio, or not yet.
audiences.context: They do not subscribe or customise. They hand over a QR code and the patient subscribes to Pelvy Lite. They need to trust the content in one look, because their name is on the recommendation.

audiences.name: People working on their pelvic floor
audiences.need: To know whether to squeeze or let go, to do it properly, and to keep it private.
audiences.context: Sent by a clinician or arriving alone. Any sex, any age: pelvic pain, pregnancy, postpartum, menopause, bladder, bowel. Often embarrassed, often overwhelmed. On a phone at home, where a notification on a lock screen is a reason to delete the app.

audiences.name: Health services and funded programs
audiences.need: Something safe to put in front of patients at scale.
audiences.context: Amelia says Pelvy cannot get into public health yet. These buyers judge a founder-led product on whether it looks like it will still be here in three years.

strategy.category: Stated: a pelvic health app that has it all. Actual: a clinician compares it with the handout and the follow-up email, and a person on their own compares it with a free Kegel timer. Chosen frame: the pelvic floor app that counts you through a program a physio set, for strength or for letting go, with your own clinician's advice beside it when you have one.

competitors.name: The handout and the follow-up email
competitors.owns: Trust, habit and zero cost. Every clinician already has them.
competitors.gap: They are lost or never opened again, they cannot count a patient through a set, and they cannot remind anyone of anything.

competitors.name: Squeezy
competitors.owns: The NHS-linked pelvic floor exercise reminder, with a professional mode for clinicians.
competitors.gap: Sold as separate apps for women and men, and built around exercise reminders rather than around the clinician's own advice.

competitors.name: Device-led trainers such as Perifit and Elvie
competitors.owns: Biofeedback and gamified strengthening, bought direct by consumers.
competitors.gap: Hardware, strengthening only, and no clinician in the loop. A person whose pelvic floor needs to relax is being sold the wrong exercise.

competitors.name: General exercise-prescription software
competitors.owns: A place in the physiotherapist's existing workflow.
competitors.gap: General purpose, not pelvic health. By Pelvy's own account these tools show a demonstration with the reps written beside it, where Pelvy counts the patient through the whole session.

strategy.positioning: For people working on their pelvic floor, with a clinician or without one yet, Pelvy is the app that counts you through the right program, strength or relaxation, and keeps the advice that goes with it, because it was built by a practising pelvic health physiotherapist who works in pelvic pain. Unlike a Kegel timer, it starts from whether you need to squeeze or to let go. Unlike a handout, it counts and it reminds. Said plainly: squeeze or let go, Pelvy counts you through what the physio set.

differentiators.claim: It does relaxation as seriously as strength: belly breathing, downtraining and contract-and-relax sit beside squeezes and holds.
It counts and cues the whole program, breath by breath, and reminds at times the person chooses.
With a subscribing physio, it carries that clinician's own programs and advice.
Without one, it gives a physio-built starting program and tells people when to go and see someone.
It is built by a practising pelvic health physiotherapist, and filmed with real people of more than one sex.
It does not keep or sell data once an account is closed.

strategy.promise: Pelvy counts you through the pelvic floor program a physio set, for strength or for letting go.

values.name: Say what it is
values.behaviour: Pelvy is education and support, not treatment, and says so. A feature that has not shipped is labelled as coming, with no date it cannot keep.

values.name: Every body
values.behaviour: Never assume the reader's sex, age or condition. Anatomy is something the person tells the app, not something the brand guesses from a colour scheme.

values.name: Plain words for private things
values.behaviour: Bladder, bowel, prolapse, sex and pain are named the way a good physiotherapist names them: once, correctly, without a euphemism and without a wink.

values.name: The clinician stays in charge
values.behaviour: Pelvy carries the clinician's plan and never competes with it. When someone is not improving, Pelvy sends them to a person.

values.name: Your information is yours
values.behaviour: Nothing is sold. When an account closes, the data is deleted, and the patient is told how to keep a copy first.

attributes.name: Matter-of-fact
attributes.meaning: Talks about a leaking bladder the way you would talk about a sore knee. The subject is ordinary, so the tone is too.

attributes.name: Steady
attributes.meaning: Counts with you and tells you where you are up to. Does not shout encouragement at someone doing a private exercise in their bedroom.

attributes.name: Knowledgeable
attributes.meaning: Explains the one thing you need to know right now, then stops. The clinician has already given the lecture.

attributes.name: Warm
attributes.meaning: Kind in what it does: a reminder you can set to say nothing at all. Never kind in the form of pet names for body parts.

attributes.name: Discreet
attributes.meaning: Careful about where words appear, on a lock screen or an envelope, and completely direct once you are inside.

personality.archetype: Caregiver, with Sage as the second voice. A drafting prompt only; guard against the Caregiver's failure of fussing over the reader.

strategy.narrative: Amelia is a pelvic health physiotherapist. She kept seeing the same thing: a patient would leave with good advice and a program, then struggle to keep up with it. The handout was lost, the email was buried, and the education was hard to find when it was needed. Patients wanted to get better. What they lacked was one place to keep it all and something to count for them. So she built Pelvy from what her patients and the clinicians around her asked for. A clinician subscribes and sets a patient up. The patient gets their clinician's advice, a program that counts every rep, and reminders they control. The clinician gets a patient who can find what they were told. Where no clinic subscribes, a GP or specialist hands over a QR code and the patient subscribes for themselves, starting on a program a physio built.

messaging.primary: Squeeze or let go. Pelvy counts you through it.

identity.schoolRationale: Jake chose it. Pelvy is one physiotherapist's care carried into an app, and this direction looks like that: today's sage, serif headings and a soft shape, kept and redrawn properly so they pass contrast and match across the website, the app and the store. The risk is that soft sage and round corners are where every wellness app lives, so three things do the identifying: the clinician's own words set large, the count, and photographs of real rooms.
identity.signature: The clinician's note: the words a clinician gave their patient, set in Literata on a sage card and signed with the clinician's name. It is the app's notes feature promoted to the brand's lead image, because it is the whole promise in one object: what your clinician told you, still with you at home.

colour.ratio: Mostly paper and white. Deep sage is the brand colour: the logo, brand text, progress, and the one main action on a view. Sage, the 2024 colour, means let go: the in-breath, relaxation content, and the quiet ground behind app screens and photographs, with ink type at 24 pixels and above only. Soft sage, a lighter step of it, is the ground for the clinician's note and anything read at text size. Slate means work: the out-breath, the squeeze and strength content, and nothing else. Ink carries the reading. White text sits on deep sage or slate, never on either sage.

logo.clearSpace: Leave clear space on every side equal to half the height of the mark. Nothing enters it: no type, no rule, no edge of the page, no other logo.

misuse.rule: Do not use the old 228 pixel image, or any screenshot of it.
misuse.why: It is the reason the logo looks soft everywhere. The vector copy replaces it.

misuse.rule: Do not bring back the gradients.
misuse.why: The flat version prints, embroiders and etches. The gradient copy is kept for reference only.

misuse.rule: Do not set the logo in the 2024 sage on white or paper.
misuse.why: The 2024 sage measures 2.9 to 1 against white. The logo is deep sage, with sage only for its lighter shapes.

misuse.rule: Do not put the white logo on either sage.
misuse.why: White on sage fails contrast. On sage the logo is ink.
The wordmark is Sulphur Point Bold, outlined, at a fixed size and position beside the symbol.

misuse.rule: Do not move the symbol, change the gap, or use the symbol to the left of the name.
misuse.why: The published arrangement is the one people know.

misuse.rule: Do not shrink the symbol under 48 pixels. Use the simplified symbol, then the small grade.
misuse.why: Its fine white lines close up and the shapes merge.

misuse.rule: Do not rotate, stretch, outline or add a shadow.
misuse.why: The figure reads as a person reaching up only when it is upright and flat.

misuse.rule: Do not use the symbol as a bullet, a pattern or a watermark over video.
misuse.why: It is a signature, used once per surface. The video thumbnails currently carry it as a watermark.

The audit found the symbol's four shapes merge to three by 16 pixels and it fails the 28 pixel icon test. Rendered, it holds from 48.
The gap between the head and the stem is the first thing to close.
Drawn on the 16 pixel grid with two pixel limbs.

provenance.generatedBy: The clean-up, redone: a vector copy of Pelvy's published 2024 symbol, fitted with smoothing splines by Claude from the 1024px app icon and the uncropped footer logo. 67 curves. Not a new design.
provenance.caveat: A generated mark is a starting point somebody approved, not a drawn one. Before it is registered or put on a building, run the similarity and trade mark searches and have a professional look at it.

logo.rationale: The logo is the one Pelvy has used since 2024: the name, then a figure reaching up whose body sweeps into the bowl of a P. Nothing about the drawing has been redesigned. It existed only as a 228 pixel image and a cropped app icon, so it has been copied into vector, shape by shape, with its edges fitted as smooth curves and the tip of the arm restored from the one file that had not cropped it. The name is set in Sulphur Point Bold, the typeface the published lettering was made with. What is new is the treatment: flat instead of graded, and in deep sage so it holds against white. A simplified symbol and a small grade, redrawn from the same figure, take over at sizes where the fine lines close up. It is a candidate until Amelia approves it.
logo.placement: Top left on the website, the deck and print, with clear space of half the symbol's height around it. Deep sage on paper and white, ink on sage, white on deep sage. Once per surface. In the app it appears on the sign-in screen and as the icon, and nowhere inside the screens.

monochrome.rule: One colour is deep sage, or black on a mono printer, or white reversed out. The lighter shapes take the same ink.
monochrome.knockout: The white lines inside the symbol are gaps in the artwork, so they stay open when it is reversed. Below 48 pixels they close, which is what the simplified symbol is for.

cobranding.rule: Beside a clinic's logo, on a set-up card or a poster, Pelvy comes second: the clinic's logo on the left, Pelvy's lockup on the right, with the line 'Your program is on Pelvy' doing the joining.
cobranding.alignment: The clinic's logo is centred on the cap height of the Pelvy wordmark.
cobranding.gap: At least the height of the Pelvy symbol between the two.
cobranding.partnerMax: The clinic's logo may be up to one and a half times the height of the Pelvy symbol. The patient knows the clinic, so the clinic leads.

imagery.direction: The app is the picture. The lead image on any Pelvy surface is a real screen from the app: the clinician's note, the count, a program. Photography is the setting around it: the corner of a home where the exercises get done, and the treatment room. Rooms, objects and hands before faces. Movement is shown with stills from the app's own exercise videos, never drawn.
imagery.treatment: Natural light, warm when it is warm: late afternoon through a curtain, morning through a clinic window. True colour, never tinted green. decisions.decision: Position Pelvy as the between-appointments companion for pelvic health care, prescribed by the clinician.
decisions.rationale: It is the one frame the evidence supports today: the clinician pays, the patient cannot yet join alone, and the shipped features (stored advice, a program that counts, reminders) are all about the time between visits. The clinician FAQ already uses the phrase once.
alternatives: The only app that has it all (the site's current line: unprovable, and half of 'all' has not shipped)
A women's wellness app (excludes half the people Pelvy is built for)
A patient-first consumer app (individuals cannot sign up yet)

decisions.decision: Draft the voice as a Caregiver with a Sage second voice, and keep the label out of the book.
decisions.rationale: It forces one character: someone who looks after you and knows the subject. The named failure to guard against is fussing over the reader, which in health copy reads as patronising.
alternatives: Sage alone (too cold for a patient at home)
Everyman (too light for a clinician deciding whether to trust it with patients)

decisions.decision: State the problem without the '20 per cent' statistic until it is sourced.
decisions.rationale: The site quotes it two ways and cites neither. Clinicians are the buyers and they check references.
alternatives: Lead the deck with the number as published

decisions.decision: Build the identity on direction A, Clinic-grade (corporate trust), with the count ring as its one repeated device.
decisions.rationale: It answers the two intake assumptions directly: buyers pick what feels bigger or safer, and the brand needs to look like it came from one place. It is also the only direction that fixes the measured contrast failures without leaning on a soft palette. Chosen without a check-in because the run was requested as autonomous; Amelia can overrule it from the territory canvas.
alternatives: B, The good physio (warm humanist): closest to today, least change, and the category's default look
C, The count (Swiss editorial): most distinctive, coldest, no gentle way to draw anatomy

decisions.decision: Pelvy green is #336841: the 2024 logo's sage at the same hue, taken from 67 to 47 per cent lightness.
decisions.rationale: The sage has two years of use behind it, so the hue stays. At its original lightness white text on it measures 2.97 to 1 and fails accessibility; deepened, it measures 6.57 to 1. The old sage survives as steps 7 and 8 of the same ramp.
alternatives: Keep sage #789F80 and put dark text on it (keeps the wellness look the brand needs to leave)
A bluer bottle green #2F6B4E as sketched in the territory round (ten degrees off the logo's own hue for no gain)

decisions.decision: One accent, Exhale amber #EFA23F, taken from the orange the app already uses for breathe out. The website's slate lavender and the app's lilac ground and purple dots are retired.
decisions.rationale: The app has already taught patients that green means in and orange means out, so the accent arrives with a meaning. Lavender and lilac pull the palette toward the pastel look of the category and carry no meaning. Amber always carries dark text, and is never the only signal: it is paired with a word.
alternatives: Keep slate lavender as the secondary
No accent at all

decisions.decision: In dark mode the mark, the ring and brand text use the light green of step 11 (#93C29D), not Pelvy green.
decisions.rationale: The system audit measured Pelvy green at 2.86 to 1 on the dark ground, too low to carry meaning. Step 11 is close to the 2024 sage, so the old colour becomes the dark-mode brand colour.
alternatives: Use Pelvy green in dark mode with a white keyline

decisions.decision: One type family: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next for display and text, Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono for counts and timers. PT Serif and DM Sans are retired.
decisions.rationale: The site's first word about itself is 'accessible', and many of the people Pelvy serves are older. Atkinson was drawn by the Braille Institute for low-vision readers, and its numerals and letters cannot be mistaken for one another, which matters in a product whose main screen is a number. One open-licensed family is also one thing for the app and the website to load, which is how they come to match.
alternatives: Keep PT Serif and DM Sans (two years of use, but the app never adopted them)
Literata and DM Sans (direction B)
Archivo (direction C)

decisions.decision: Build the identity on direction B, The good physio (warm humanist). This replaces d4, and with it d5 to d8.
decisions.rationale: Jake picked it from the territory canvas. It keeps the most of what Pelvy has spent two years building (the sage, serif headings, DM Sans) and fixes the execution. The named risk still stands and is managed in the system: soft sage and round corners are the wellness category's default, so the identifying work is done by the one-line figures, the writing and real photography, and no text is ever set white on sage.
alternatives: A, Clinic-grade (corporate trust): the working choice made before Jake had seen the sketches
C, The count (Swiss editorial)

decisions.decision: Three colours and a paper. Deep sage #41684A is the brand solid; Sage #78A080, the 2024 colour, is kept for large fills under dark text; Slate #5E6687 is the one accent. This replaces d5 and d6.
decisions.rationale: Deep sage is the logo's own sage at the same hue and chroma, taken from 67 to 48 per cent lightness, so white text on it measures 6.36 to 1 where the original measured 2.97. The original sage stays in the system because two years of use is worth keeping, with the rule that only dark text sits on it. Slate is the website's lavender button colour deepened until white text passes at 5.64 to 1. The app's orange, lilac ground and purple dots are retired so the app and the website finally share one palette.
alternatives: Sage as the solid with dark text on buttons (keeps the exact colour, but every button becomes low-contrast against paper)
Exhale amber as the accent, from the app's breathe-out state (direction A)

decisions.decision: Literata for headings, DM Sans for text, DM Mono for counts and timers. PT Serif is retired. This replaces d8.
decisions.rationale: The serif-heading, sans-body pairing is what the site has used since 2024 and it stays. PT Serif goes because the site asks it for a medium weight it does not have, so headings fall back to regular; Literata is a variable face built for reading on screens, with the weights and optical sizes to work on a phone and on a poster. DM Sans is already the site's text face and becomes the app's too, which is how the two come to match. All three are open-licensed.
alternatives: Keep PT Serif (two years of use, two weights, no optical sizes)
Atkinson Hyperlegible Next throughout (direction A)

decisions.decision: In dark mode the mark and brand text use step 11 of the ramp (#9BBFA2), not deep sage. This replaces d7.
decisions.rationale: The audit measured deep sage at 2.96 to 1 on the dark ground. Step 11 is close to the 2024 sage and reads clearly.
alternatives: Deep sage with a light keyline

decisions.decision: Pelvy does not illustrate. The one-line figure sketched in direction B is dropped, and the signature becomes the clinician's note, with the count ring beside it.
decisions.rationale: Checked against the three audiences. Clinicians prescribe from video and anatomy and judge exercise content on precision, which a faceless line figure cannot give; the central exercise is internal and cannot be drawn at all. Patients already get real video and the count in the app. Health services do not buy on illustration. A figure would therefore be decoration, and decoration is what makes a clinical tool read as a consumer wellness app. The note and the count are real objects from the product, and each explains half of what Pelvy does.
alternatives: Keep the one-line figure as the signature (as sketched)
Keep a small set of position icons (lying, sitting, kneeling, standing) in the same line: possibly useful in the exercise library, not tested here

decisions.decision: The voice is derived from Pelvy's own published writing, and two of its five attributes are changes, not descriptions.
decisions.rationale: Plain about bodies, honest about limits and reasoned are already how the site and FAQs write. Steady (no cheerleading, no exclamation marks) and specific (no capitals, no superlatives) describe the app's exercise screens and the pricing answers, but not the website's headlines, so for marketing copy they are a decision to change. Confidence is medium: seven pieces of site and store copy, none of it email, SMS or review replies, and it is not confirmed that Amelia wrote all of it.
alternatives: Document the site's current voice as it is, capitals and exclamation marks included

decisions.decision: The app is the hero of every surface. The proof set starts with four app screens redrawn in the system, and every other piece leads with one of them.
decisions.rationale: Jake's steer: anything Pelvy shows is really promoting the app. The review agreed: the app already holds the two objects that explain the product (the clinician's note and the count) and real exercise video, and it is also where the brand is least consistent today, with its own green, an orange, a lilac ground and neither of the website's typefaces.
alternatives: Lead with photography and treat the app as one application among ten

decisions.decision: In the app, breathing in is a filled sage disc and breathing out is the same disc emptied to a pale tint with an outline. The orange is retired.
decisions.rationale: Full on the in-breath and empty on the out-breath is a difference of shape, so it survives colour blindness and greyscale, and the words 'Breathe in' and 'Breathe out' are always there. The app's orange cue text on its lilac ground measured well under the contrast floor, and orange appears nowhere else in the brand.
alternatives: Slate for the out-breath (uses the accent twice on one screen)
Keep the orange as a product-only colour

decisions.decision: The mark is concept T1w from logo round 2.
decisions.rationale: Generated against a planned concept brief and measured against the application context matrix. NOBODY HAS APPROVED IT YET, and it must not be published as the mark until somebody has.
alternatives: the other concepts in the round, kept under brand/logo/concepts

decisions.decision: The candidate mark is T1w: the 2024 figure redrawn flat at one even weight, with the name in DM Sans 600 to its right.
decisions.rationale: Five refinements of a trace of the published app icon were drawn and measured. T1w cleared every audit test, holds at small sizes, and sits comfortably beside a medium-weight sans. T1p keeps more of the original's brush taper and is thinner at small sizes; T1sq was ruled out at favicon size; T1c is the faithful clean-up and fails the app icon tests. The symbol moves from the right of the name to the left, which is where an app icon and a website header expect it. Not approved by a person yet: recorded as a candidate.
alternatives: T1p, proportion (closest to the original's brush character)
T1sq, the square alternate
T1c, the trace cleaned up
Keep the 2024 raster logo and commission a vector redraw

decisions.decision: Reposition from 'between appointments, prescribed by the clinician' to 'the pelvic floor app that counts you through a physio-set program, for strength or for letting go'. This replaces d1.
decisions.rationale: The demo video Jake supplied shows Pelvy Lite: people can subscribe without a clinic, and GPs and specialists are being asked to recommend it. The old frame described one of three routes in. Strength and relaxation, counted, is true of all three, and it is the difference from a Kegel timer. 'Between appointments' stays as the line for the physiotherapy channel.
alternatives: Keep the between-appointments frame and treat Lite as a side door
Two separate brands, Pelvy and Pelvy Lite

decisions.decision: Sage means let go and slate means work, in the player and in the content. Hold is a ring. This replaces d16.
decisions.rationale: The next version marks breathe in, breathe out and hold in green, orange and blue, and tags content as relaxation or strength in purple and orange, with three more hues elsewhere. Those are two real distinctions wearing eight colours. The system carries them with its own two: sage for the in-breath, letting go and relaxation content, slate for the out-breath, the squeeze and strength content, and an empty deep sage ring for hold. Each state also differs in lightness and carries its word, so it survives colour blindness.
alternatives: Keep orange and blue as product-only state colours
Distinguish states by shape alone, with no second colour

decisions.decision: The mark is concept T1c from logo round 2.
decisions.rationale: Generated against a planned concept brief and measured against the application context matrix. NOBODY HAS APPROVED IT YET, and it must not be published as the mark until somebody has.
alternatives: the other concepts in the round, kept under brand/logo/concepts

decisions.decision: The working logo is the 2024 logo itself, copied exactly into vector and made flat in deep sage, with the name in its original typeface, Sulphur Point Bold. The redraw (T1w) becomes the simplified symbol for small sizes. This replaces d18.
decisions.rationale: Jake asked for the copy to be smooth, to match the published logo and to be shown in colour so it could be checked. Done carefully, the copy is good enough to be the logo: direction B is about keeping what exists and making it properly, and this keeps the drawing, the arrangement and the lettering. The audit rules the exact symbol out under 28 pixels, where its shapes merge, so the simpler redraw and the 16 pixel grade take over there. Not approved by a person yet: recorded as a candidate.
alternatives: T1w, the even-weight redraw, as the logo at every size, with the name in DM Sans
Keep the gradients
Keep the 2024 sage as the logo colour

decisions.decision: Main actions are deep sage. Slate is not a button colour: it means work, and appears only on the out-breath, the squeeze and strength content. This amends d10 and d20.
decisions.rationale: Once slate was given a meaning in the app, using it for 'Book a demo' and 'Subscribe' as well would have made it mean two things. The generated tokens already make the primary button the brand colour, so this also keeps the artboards and the tokens a developer receives in step.
alternatives: Slate for every primary action, as in the direction B sketch
A third colour for actions

decisions.decision: Brought the last clinic-only lines in line with the positioning: the purpose, the story, the Pelvy Lite non-goal, the money rule and one voice example.
decisions.rationale: An adversarial pass found five live fields still written for the brand before Pelvy Lite: a non-goal that put self-subscribers on a waitlist, a money rule quoting the retired $99 price, and a voice example telling people they need a participating clinician. Each contradicted Pelvy's own March 2026 demo, and the book prints them.
alternatives: Leave them and flag them in the handover
Remove the fields

openQuestions.question: Intake 1: what are we doing here, tidying up or replacing?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Decides whether the existing logo, green and typefaces are constraints or candidates for retirement.
openQuestions.assumedMeanwhile: Modernising. Keep the equity that has been accumulating (the name, the sage green family, the figure that makes a P) and replace the execution (raster gradient logo, template website, stock illustration, the app and site not matching). Brief said 'modernising her brand end to end'; intake was not asked because the run was requested as autonomous.
openQuestions.changesIf: If Amelia wants a clean break, the green and the figure are released and the Identity phase reruns from the logo forge. If she wants the logo untouched, the redrawn mark is dropped and the existing artwork needs a professional vector redraw before anything is printed. Show her the proof canvas and ask which.

openQuestions.question: Intake 2: where does most of the work actually come from today?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Decides the application set and which surfaces get proven.
openQuestions.assumedMeanwhile: A referral partner: clinicians subscribe and put their patients on Pelvy, and Amelia recruits clinics herself by demo. Inferred from the site: individuals cannot yet join without a clinician, and she onboards every clinic manually. So the proof set leads with the clinician demo deck, the app store profile, and the card a clinician hands a patient.
openQuestions.changesIf: If most sign-ups are actually arriving from Instagram or search, add a Story artboard and a search listing and move the deck down. Ask her where the last ten clinics heard of Pelvy.

openQuestions.question: Intake 3: when a clinic or a health service picks something else, why?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Decides whether the job is differentiation or being credible enough to be considered.
openQuestions.assumedMeanwhile: They pick what feels bigger or safer: an established exercise-prescription platform, an NHS-backed app such as Squeezy, or paper handouts they already trust. Pelvy is a founder-led pilot asking for a place inside hospital and clinic workflows, so the identity has to read as clinically serious before it reads as friendly.
openQuestions.changesIf: If the real answer is price or 'never heard of you', the craft budget moves from credibility to reach. Ask her what the last three clinics that said no gave as their reason.

openQuestions.question: Intake 4: a year from now, which matters most?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Decides where the craft budget goes.
openQuestions.assumedMeanwhile: Everything looks like it came from the same place. The website, the app and the store listing currently use three different greens, two type systems and an orange and a purple that appear nowhere else. A developer getting it right first time is the close second, because the app is built by someone other than Amelia.
openQuestions.changesIf: If she would rather be able to charge more, more goes into photography and materials and less into tokens. Confirm with her.

openQuestions.question: Is the '20% of what clinicians say' figure sourced?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: The whole problem statement leans on it, and the site says both 'less than 20%' remembered and 'up to 80%' forgotten without a citation. A health brand quoting an unsourced statistic to clinicians is a credibility risk.
openQuestions.assumedMeanwhile: A real study sits behind it and Amelia can name it. Until she does, brand copy states the problem without the number.
openQuestions.changesIf: With a citation, the figure can lead the clinician deck. Without one, it stays out of every headline. Ask her for the paper.

openQuestions.question: Are the three testimonials and sixteen client logos on the home page real?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: They read as template placeholders (Courtney Henry, Cody Fisher, Devon Lane; Asgardia, Aven, Circle). On a health product that is a trust problem, and no brand copy can quote them.
openQuestions.assumedMeanwhile: They are leftovers from the website template and are not Pelvy customers.
openQuestions.changesIf: If any are real, they can be quoted with permission. If not, remove them from the live site now; this does not need to wait for the rebrand.

openQuestions.question: Does Amelia hold the original logo artwork as a vector, and who drew it?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Only a 228px raster and a 1024px app icon are public. A redrawn mark needs her approval and, if a designer drew the original, a check on who owns it.
openQuestions.assumedMeanwhile: No vector exists and Amelia owns the artwork outright. The modernised mark in this system is a new drawing built on the same idea, proposed for her approval, not a trace of the old file.
openQuestions.changesIf: If a vector exists, compare it with the redrawn master before choosing. If a third party owns the original, get the assignment in writing before the new mark ships.

openQuestions.question: What may Pelvy claim clinically, given it is not TGA certified?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Voice and messaging have to stay inside 'education and support between appointments' and never promise treatment or outcomes. The wrong verb on a poster is a regulatory problem, not a style one.
openQuestions.assumedMeanwhile: Pelvy can say it guides, reminds, stores and educates. It does not say it treats, diagnoses, fixes or cures, and it does not promise symptom improvement.
openQuestions.changesIf: If Pelvy is later listed with the TGA, the vocabulary list is revisited. Have the claims list in the voice chapter checked by whoever advises her on TGA and AHPRA advertising rules before print.

openQuestions.question: How unique is the figure-P symbol, and is sage green ownable, among pelvic health and women's health apps?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: The symbol is named as the lead distinctive asset and the green as a supporting one. Neither has been checked against the category.
openQuestions.assumedMeanwhile: The figure is unique enough to keep. Soft sage is shared across wellness brands, so the system deepens it and pairs it with the count ring instead of relying on it alone.
openQuestions.whoCanAnswer: Jake or Amelia, with twenty minutes
openQuestions.changesIf: If three or more competitors use a figure built from an initial, the count ring becomes the lead asset. Screenshot the icons of the first twenty results for 'pelvic floor' on the App Store and lay them in a grid beside Pelvy's.

openQuestions.question: Is 'five times the adherence' backed by data, and how many clinicians are subscribed today?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Amelia says both in her demo video. They are the two most persuasive facts Pelvy has for a GP or a health service, and neither can be printed without a source and a date.
openQuestions.assumedMeanwhile: Both are true as she stated them in March 2026. Neither appears in any artboard or in the tagline until she supplies the numbers behind them.
openQuestions.changesIf: With a source, 'five times' leads the clinician deck and the one-pager. Ask her what was measured, over how long, in how many patients.

openQuestions.question: Do clinic-subscribed patients still get the Clinician Notes card in the version with the Programs, Videos and Learn tabs, and where does it sit?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: The clinician's note is the brand's signature. The demo shows the Lite path, where there is no clinician and no note.
openQuestions.assumedMeanwhile: Yes: for a clinic patient the note sits above the programs on the Programs tab, as in the current store screenshots. In Lite its place is taken by Amelia's own guidance in Learn.
openQuestions.changesIf: If notes have moved or gone, the hub artboard is redrawn and the signature leans on the Learn articles instead. Ask for a screen recording of a clinic patient's hub.

openQuestions.question: Should the tagline stay 'Pelvic health, between appointments' now that people can use Pelvy without a clinician?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: It describes the physiotherapy route exactly and the Lite route only loosely.
openQuestions.assumedMeanwhile: It stays, as the line for clinics and clinicians. Patient-facing surfaces lead with 'Squeeze or let go. Pelvy counts you through it.'
openQuestions.changesIf: If she wants one line everywhere, the candidates are 'Strength and relaxation for your pelvic floor' and the squeeze-or-let-go line. Put both on the store listing for a fortnight each and compare installs.

openQuestions.question: Are the clinic price ($20 a month in the pilot), the six free months for patients and the word 'pilot' still current?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: The voice chapter rewrites real pricing copy from the clinician FAQ. The patient FAQ on the same site is already out of date against the app, so the clinic numbers may be too, and a wrong price in print is the costly kind of mistake.
openQuestions.assumedMeanwhile: Treated as current because pelvy.app/clinician-faqs still publishes them. Check with Amelia before any clinic price is printed.

nonGoals: Renaming Pelvy, or changing the idea behind the symbol.
Redesigning the app's flows. This system gives the app its colours, type and components; what each screen does is product work.
Clinical content. The education and exercise library are Amelia's, and nothing here rewrites them.
A regulatory review. The claims guidance in the voice chapter is a writing rule, not legal or TGA advice.
A separate identity for Pelvy Lite. People who subscribe themselves and people set up by a clinic get the same brand.
antiPatterns: White text on sage. It is how Pelvy looked in 2024, how every wellness app looks, and it fails contrast at 2.9 to 1.
Pink or coral anywhere, and the app's lilac ground and purple dots. They say women's wellness, and Pelvy is for everyone with a pelvis.
Icons in pastel circles, in rows of three.
Illustrated people of any kind: stock, flat, faceless or line-drawn. A drawing cannot show a pelvic floor exercise, so Pelvy shows the real app, real video and real rooms.
A clinician's note that nobody wrote. A note is real and used with permission, or it is marked as a sample.
A count ring holding anything except a numeral that is really counting something.
A fourth radius. Panels and photographs take 22 pixels, buttons are pills, fields take 10.
A testimonial, client logo or statistic that Amelia cannot source.
The words treat, cure, fix or diagnose.
CAPITALS for emphasis and exclamation marks to carry enthusiasm.
